notes.title: Multiplayer | Devlog #4
notes.content:
[h1]🔔[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2[/url]🔔[/h1][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Hey there Escapists!

Last week we had a [u][url="https://steamcommunity.com/games/3296060/announcements/detail/538864124750202555"]blog on multiplayer systems[/url][/u] - the super cool stuff that’ll help you get along with your teammate a little better - outlines, pings, and emotes! However, we wanted to dedicate a blog to go over the concept of multiplayer as a whole, how it’s shaping up for [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School[/url][/u], and some of what you can expect.[/p][h1]Not enough time to read?[/h1][p align="start"]That’s okay. Luckily for you, we’ve got that handled. Check out our YouTube devlog on multiplayer![/p][p align="start"][/p][h1]Why Good Multiplayer is Important[/h1][p align="start"]Escape Academy 1’s multiplayer was exactly what you’d expect out of a co-op escape room experience: you could give your partner items, and they existed in the same space as you while you solved puzzles. This did its job well, as you wouldn’t be exploring larger areas, but during some playtests for Escape Academy 2, we realized that multiplayer needed some upgrades.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h1]Our Process[/h1][p align="start"][u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy 1[/url][/u] taught us that playtesting is incredibly important. Just look at these internal documents I “borrowed” from our [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/6609cfbd85bb33d94f7fa05b1ce45de7cb5ac6cd.png"][/img]retrospective last year![/p][p][/p][p align="start"]While we were playtesting, we found a couple of issues with multiplayer that made it a little difficult for players to get the full experience out of an open-world game. But, we were missing something.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/9482a433b523336a0bee0775d719d6d330c4c271.png"][/img][/p][p]When it comes to [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url][/u], our pool of playtesters is [i]much[/i] larger and we’re making sure to use this to our advantage. With the first game, we let it fall behind for the reasons listed above, and this led to some of our puzzles in the later portions of the game losing the consistency we built with the early portions of the game. You might not have even noticed this as a player, but to us as a studio, it was leagues of difference.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/bcdb6be3cd22ab3f87e4236d982ad1eac151187f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Consistent playtesting has led us to be a lot happier, and much more confident, when it comes to our puzzle/world design with [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url][/u]. Now, whenever we’re making something, we try not to call it fun until we’ve seen another player have fun with it. And even then, we want to playtest it over and over again to make sure that what we’re seeing is genuine enjoyment out of puzzle lovers like us.[/p][p align="start"]Playtesting has been a huge help for building out our open-world multiplayer.[/p][p][/p][h1][i]Open-World[/i] Multiplayer[/h1][p align="start"]A large campus brings large demands. Meet Player 1 and Player 2 - two of our playtesters here to help demonstrate how we came to the addition of the new multiplayer systems we introduced in our last blog.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/f6887c1eadbadfd177a2c6b27d2dbbb99f01b58f.png"][/img][/p][p]Nice to meet you, Player 1 and Player 2! Let’s take a look at how your playtests went.[/p][p][/p][h1]Challenge 1:[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/27b03cd1bb0e984d9f650047d644c847c11cd7e5.png"][/img][/p][p]Player 1 is not the best when it comes to descriptive language - but Player 2 has the projector still that leads to one of the 3 answers needed for this puzzle. So, Player 1 says:

”I think you can put that projector still in that projector over there”

But Player 2 is beyond lost. “Over where? I don’t see it!” Well, it’s certainly not on the ceiling.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Thanks to Player 2, Escape Academy now has pings for the first time ever.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/146b563d6670a74617676ebd8e7447eedd7110c4.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Challenge 2:[/h1][p align="start"]Both players just finished an escape room. Great! But now they’re just standing there. Menacingly. Soullessly.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/18d1ca2755b9f761b992dc43062c15a40c05a229.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]However, our brand-new WIP emotes system is bound to fix that and give Player 1 and Player 2 an outlet to let out some of that extra energy. Let’s celebrate![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/1600e50c74e5a8ebf945326d8e9fa4190749aa9c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Challenge 3:[/h1][p align="start"]Lastly, it’s easy to get lost in an open world campus. You might be able to meet up in a designated spot on campus, or just learn the map, but to us, being able to keep a close eye on your partner makes staying together a little bit easier.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Now, no matter where you are, you can keep a close eye on your partner. Whether they know it or not.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/b67c6cc8e543250bc31c2bb00b9f6a4f177973e0.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h1]My Fun Is Not Your Fun[/h1][p align="start"]Lastly, one of the biggest lessons we learned while making multiplayer, and subsequently playtesting the multiplayer experience, is that fun is subjective. I won’t go too deep into this here because it’s quite the lengthy topic and this blog is already quite tall, but if you want to see a talk on this, [u][url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGpFEv1-mAo"]Gabe Newell has an excellent interview with a behavioural psychologist where he talks all about it.[/url][/u][/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]Regardless, playtesting has taught us a lot about what “fun” is, and as compared to Escape Academy 1, we’ve made a vow to ourselves to not call something fun until we’ve seen someone else have fun with it first.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h1]See you next time![/h1][p align="start"]Hopefully you’re excited for multiplayer too - but what you see here isn’t the end of the road for us. We want your suggestions! If you have anything on your “Escape Academy 2’s Multiplayer Wishlist”, please let us know in the comments and we’ll take a deeper look at it![/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]If you’re excited about multiplayer too, make sure to let us know by [b][i][u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]putting us on your wishlist[/url][/u][/i][/b]. And if you made it here, thank you for reading.

With love,[/p][p align="start"]Coin Crew Games💛💜[/p][p][/p][h1] 🔔[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2[/url]🔔[/h1]

notes.title: Multiplayer Systems | Devlog #3
notes.content: [h1][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]🔔WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2: BACK 2 SCHOOL!🔔[/url][/h1][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Hey Escapists![/p][p align="start"]We hope you enjoyed our [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YumDGaGDJGg&ab_channel=CoinCrewGames"]first longform devlog on YouTube[/url]; expect another one soon! 👀[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]One of our favourite staples of Escape Academy 1 was the multiplayer interactions that led to silly moments, or gave way to fun conversations with players. Bringing people together is fun! [url="https://www.coincrew.games/"]I mean, it’s even in our motto[/url].[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]So far, we’ve had a few questions on the topic of multiplayer interactions:[/p][list][*][p]Will there be online multiplayer?[/p][/*][*][p]Splitscreen couch co-op? 🥺[/p][/*][*][p]Toggleable splitscreen?[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]To put the answers shortly:[/p][h1]YES! [i]and…[/i][/h1][p align="start"]There’s also a couple of things we’re adding to change up the way duos will explore the Academy - both to help with interacting in an open world, and to make the multiplayer experience that much more interesting.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Let’s take a look 🧐[/p][h1]What’s Different?[/h1][p align="start"]It’s a bird! It’s a plane! It’s a….[b][i]ping?[/i][/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/10bbfe2124dadbfc402bcc6b601ae11263729f62.png"][/img][/p][p]When it comes to an escape room, things are a lot more localized. You can say “Hey, come check this out!” and walk a few feet over to your partner. Maybe your duo will point out something “[b][i]over there, by that desk.[/i][/b]” But when you’re exploring a giant sprawling campus, “over there” becomes a bit….confusing. Pings have quickly become a staple in many multiplayer experiences, and we think that bringing them into the world of Escape Academy will help make solving puzzles together less frustrating, while also leading to some silly interactions.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/2277986f943d23d8e3bc2feafe1aded0f510a72d.png"][/img][/p][h1]What if I get lost?[/h1][p align="start"]That’s a fair argument. If you’ve been keeping up with our devlogs and short-form content, it’s a very real concern. Escape Academy is the leading academy in the art of Escape, after all![/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]While many multiplayer games might opt to leash you within a certain range of the first player, we don’t want players to be limited to any single area - that can take away from the open world experience. So instead, cutting-edge Academy technology will allow you to see where your partner is on campus at any given point![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/f71fe89423515b2fbf8edb773b96809801473d7c.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Still struggling to find eachother?[/b] That’s okay. The gazebo in the middle of campus is an excellent place to relax and meet up before planning your next escape.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/90ceb385a4b7115ce3b6e13a8bf22dd1c9de2d48.png"][/img][/p][h1]Emotes🥳💃[/h1][p]Every good Escapist needs a way to express themselves. We’re bringing emotes to Escape Academy as a way to help players communicate, for the better or for the worse. Solved that difficult puzzle? That deserves a thumbs up! Struggling with a spinner lock? Seems like the perfect opportunity for a sarcastic clap.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/ed3695796825988e3676e595c7bfce20974f8a66.png"][/img][/p][h1]What else?[/h1][p align="start"]One of the complaints from playtesters we’ve gotten is that splitscreen modes in online gameplay can be a little disorienting. So, just like in Escape Academy 1, you’ll have the option to switch between the splitscreen and widescreen views if motion sickness is something that affects you.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/e6611761ece3f3be32b5c5e42ebbae53e6ab780b.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Partner taking a little too long to unpause in couch co-op? Time to take things into your own hands.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/7546d425b6969614d093ba02846d9fb09957fe29.png"][/img][/p][p]Lastly, to keep things from being a little too janky (or asking for a little too much out of your computer), players will have to enter escape rooms together. Always remember that two minds are better than one! Usually.[/p][p][/p][h1]See you in the next one![/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/94d7eaff66b82734043c6f5dd335d683e9eedde6.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re hoping multiplayer features will give [i]just[/i] the right amount of sass to multiplayer interactions, and help to immerse you in the world of Escape Academy a little bit. If you have anything on your wishlist for Escape Academy 2 features, just let us know in the comments![/p][p][/p][p]That’s all from us - [i]for now. [/i]Stay tuned for another longform devlog coming soon, and don’t forget to…[/p][h1][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]🔔WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2: BACK 2 SCHOOL!🔔[/url][/h1][p][/p][p]With Love,[/p][p align="start"]Coin Crew Games💛💜[/p]

notes.title: How Did We Get Here? | Devlog #2
notes.content:
[p]Welcome back, Escapists![/p][p] [/p][p]We’re here again this week with another devlog, this time digging deeper at some stuff from behind the scenes - despite some sneak peeks at our quests system here and some short-form content there, you might catch yourself wondering:[/p][h1]How Did We Get Here?[/h1][p]Let’s go back. Waaaay back. Our studio, [url="https://www.coincrew.games/"]Coin Crew Games[/url], was founded in 2018 with one simple goal in mind: to bring people together through play. It started with arcade cabinets, and over time as we grew as a team, we started to branch out with some other goals in mind. With the ongoing pandemic in 2020, we were led to [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy[/url]’s conception - our first full-fledged puzzle video game that could be played by anyone, anywhere, in your own home.[/p][p] [/p][p]Staring at the Steam store, our [b]co-founder Wyatt[/b] recounts: “[i]…We didn't see any local co-op escape room games on the store pages. As a team, we love local co-op games like Towerfall, Speedrunners, and Overcooked are all games that we really enjoy playing, so there not being a solid escape room version felt like a gap in the market.[/i]” It was a daunting project, and the co-op elements meant you could play with your friends and family from a distance. Given that arcade games were supposed to last a few minutes before being replayed, which was challenging enough to make, a gameplay experience for [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy[/url] that would last 4-6 hours was an exciting [b][i]and[/i][/b] intimidating task.[/p][p] [/p][p]Over the next couple years, we would put thousands of hours into the creation of [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy[/url]. After mountains of effort and learning, we could finally put down our pencils and say that it was finished. However, at this point it was time to take our vision a step further.[/p][h1]Starting A Sequel[/h1][p][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School[/url] has been in development for nearly a year now. In that time we’ve been using all the lessons that Escape Academy 1 gave us - one of the most important of those lessons being that we made [i]just about[/i] every mistake you can make in the design of our original game engine.[/p][p] [/p][p]Given our ambitions going into the sequel, and wanting to avoid inheriting the bugs from the first engine, we had to make a difficult decision. That’s why before we could even get started with 2, it was time to burn down the first engine and start completely over. So, we were here:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/14c30a127962989c27f3d6056c4c1814e3f4cda1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]It was a blessing [b]and[/b] a curse, in many different ways. Starting over meant, well, [i]starting from nothing[/i]. But starting over [b]also[/b] meant we could use those lessons we learned from the [i]first[/i] game to build bigger and even better.[/p][p] [/p][p][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url] started as two pictures:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/f7ff91f0eb579d746077eac51aa89819eb13c683.png"][/img][/p][p]It would be an open world experience where you could talk to NPCs and be taken through quests and puzzle rooms while exploring a whimsical academy that teaches the art of escape. It evolved to a collection of questions, that went something like this:[/p][p] [/p][list][*][p][i]How do we make a sequel?[/i][/p][list][*][p]We know that we don’t want Escape Academy 1.5. We want [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url]. A sequel shouldn’t feel like a bunch of extra level packs, but rather be a completely transformative take on the world of Escape Academy.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][i]Is this possible?[/i][/p][list][*][p]There’s [b]open-world games[/b], and there’s [b]escape room games[/b]. But this time, we’re doing [b]both[/b] - how does one accomplish that?[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][i]How do open-world mechanics change a puzzle game?[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]How can we learn from the mistakes we made in the past?[/i][/p][/*][/list][p][i]Don’t let these questions fool you[/i] - [i]every[/i] answer would have a [b]counterargument[/b], and every point has its own [b]counterpoint[/b]. Plenty of ideas would be thrown around, some kept, some scrapped, and we watched as the world of Escape Academy itself evolved with our ideas.[/p][p] [/p][p]Now, it was time to begin [i]prototyping[/i].[/p][h1]The Prototype[/h1][p]The first (and completely, totally sane) version of our game looked something like this:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/300e22eb9d8c1b9718981d012ffeb564e98d8b8c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We had this idea for a first escape room where you have to escape from detention, and so we assembled a super basic test environment that allowed us to see what that might be like. We were pretty much trying to get an idea of how our new engine was working, because in these early stages there’s always bugs and problems you need to look out for. In these polished devlogs, you don’t always get to see the trials and tribulations that game development really can be - but trust me - the team has had our fair share of late night troubleshooting, even back then.[/p][p] [/p][p]This also happened to be the point in our development process where we introduced the quests system - If you’ve read our last blog post ([url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3296060/view/538860320326680900?l=english"]which you definitely should, by the way[/url]) you’ll notice it looks a lot different here![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/74ee2d04eab2f77a63886e1dc94359775a9a3e70.png"][/img][/p][p] [/p][h1]Building The Campus[/h1][p]Now that we’d nailed down a prototype and had our game engine in a spot we were happy with, we could start thinking about what an open-world escape room experience would truly look like.[/p][p] [/p][p]3 weeks of combined engineering, design, narrative, and art efforts led us here! This is one of the earliest stages of the campus you’ll see, and this foundation was a glorious first step.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/fd721e1459bbaf3781fd0a86f86da911f7eeb40f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Past this point, we started to think of the first areas that could be interesting to design escape rooms in, especially now that we could start visualizing how quests would function - maybe you run from that tower overlooking everything to the dome over on the right. We set our sights on Humanities - the section of the Academy where you’d learn about the history and culture of Escape.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/fa89d5f6b12532593dcdd458d043b737a1c8f53f.png"][/img][/p][p]This area was incredibly impactful to the team, because we were finally getting into the big chunks of open-world gameplay that players would experience. We designed our first big puzzles for Escape Academy 2 here, and if you’ve seen our [url="https://www.youtube.com/shorts/B-xvxIkxyts"]viral Aztec Lock video[/url], this area will end up being very familiar👀[/p][p]The Humanities area also marked the point where research began to play a major part in our process. When designing puzzles, we would often find ourselves miles-deep in research rabbitholes trying to find interesting ways to tie puzzles in to other cultures, and fun ways to tie the Escape Academy lore/history into our puzzles as well. It was a very educational process for the entire team, especially because we were getting back into the swing of things with game development after Escape Academy. Humanities got to stretch beyond just a campus area - it became a massive milestone marker of what our hard work had become![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/d9b8c134582b9be1070e377a64ad8f51de2a4f3f.gif"][/img][/p][p]                                  I don’t think I remember Escape Bucks looking like that…[/p][p][/p][p]At this time in our development process, we began to swap between escape room design and open-world design because often times, an escape room would demand something from our open-world environment or vice versa. Sometimes we’d go back and change things because narrative would change, or maybe something wouldn’t play how we wanted. Months and months of work later, our process would lead us here: we created the Headmaster’s Tower as you know it, in all its glory![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/7e5b3e4f062ad4df7a2e8c2802dd070913726ee6.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Don’t be fooled![/h1][p]Don’t let these quick snapshots into our development process make you think it was easy - game design is hard, and what you’re seeing is nearly a [i]year[/i] of combined efforts from a team of around ten people. We’re incredibly grateful for those of you who have been following us, because keeping this exciting project secret for almost a year was not easy.[/p][p] [/p][p]Next week, we plan to dive a little deeper into all of this on our [url="https://www.youtube.com/@coincrewgames/featured"]YouTube channel[/url] and really give you a thorough look at what the timeline up to Humanities was like for us - but we hope this teaser has satiated your curiosity for now😉[/p][p] [/p][p]What are you dying to know in the development process? When it comes to these devlogs, what speaks most to you? Let us know in the comments![/p][p]And as always, don’t forget to:[/p][h1][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]🔔WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2🔔[/url][/h1][p]and we’ll see you in the next one.[/p][p] [/p][p]With Love,[/p][p]Coin Crew Games💛💜[/p]

notes.title: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School Devlog #1 - Quests!
notes.content: [p][i]Dear Escapists[/i],[/p][p]You read that right. Welcome to our first devlog; a series where we’ll be taking a dive into some of the things we’re dreaming up for [i][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School[/url][/i]. Our work-in-progress quest system is the first system (of many!) we’re excited to show you.[/p][p][/p][h1]Why Quests?[/h1][p]From a top-down perspective, [b]critical quests[/b] and escape rooms advance you through the story and important narrative events, while [b]side quests[/b] allow for a natural way to interact with the campus environment and other students. That’s not to say side quests won’t reward you for your hard work, though![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/43cd6217a67f0b2c1dfc725e6cfd72873f48ce00.png"][/img][/p][p]When it comes to quests, there are two types: critical path and side quests, and it’s taken a lot of trial-and-error to reach that point.[/p][p]We want the side quests to be obvious enough that you don’t miss them, secret enough that you feel rewarded when you encounter them, and clear enough that you don’t end up doing a side quest on accident when you want to progress the story. So, we’ve found ourselves tweaking things as small as wording in text, lighting, etc. to draw the player’s attention in [i]just the right way[/i] without being too obvious or intrusive.[/p][p]                [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/05b33fcb833d4fe83334769f02f8dec283b63920.png"][/img][/p][p]               These are just a few of the quest-givers you’ll find throughout the Academy…🔒[/p][p]                                Blue Icon = Critical Path | Red Icon = Extra Credit! 🔥[/p][p][/p][p]One of my personal favorite things about quests is that they let the entire world be littered with puzzles instead of rooms, which in my opinion gives so much more life and personality to the campus. Here are some of the questions you might have about the upcoming quests system (feel free to drop your own in the comments!):[/p][p] [/p][h1]What makes quests meaningful?[/h1][p]Currently, we have quests that progress the main story, and some quests that are optional. (In our demo build, you can go on a quest to bring food to the cat in your dorm, and have a furry friend that follows you around!)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/e4f71c11b2fa0a2a214825b0b2b052fe7c844610.png"][/img]              Maybe having a cat isn't [i]required[/i], but it's definitely a gameplay-enhancer on all fronts.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/a760dc56ae585206a96103c0d3691e8bdda3ffe7.png"][/img][/p][p]Unlike Escape Academy 1, [i][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url] [/i]will have a fully-fleshed out campus that you can explore to your heart’s content. One of the benefits of an open-world campus is that there’s many more opportunities for narrative.[/p][p]That’s one of the biggest reasons we chose to implement this[i] [/i]system, and we know you’ll love to explore the world at your own pace while uncovering the secrets of Escape Academy in a rewarding, fully-immersive environment. Quests help so much with this effort, because you end up with a nudge forward, without feeling like you’re solving puzzles “just because”.[/p][p] [/p][p]For quests that don’t directly contribute to the main story, we still want quests to be rewarding and meaningful, which is why a lot of these side quests will be tied to a system called…[/p][h1]Escape Bucks![/h1][p]Escape Bucks are a currency (don’t worry, no microtransactions here) that enables you to travel around campus in various ways. Maybe you spend 3 Escape Bucks to bribe the librarian, or drop 1 Escape Buck into the vending machine for a can of ESCAPIST’S EDGE![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/0671e5b0cf670f440c1fd04a4a2bacd74744fa3e.png"][/img][/p][p]From a game-design perspective, we love the Escape Bucks system, because it introduces a fictional currency that makes side quests feel more rewarding. Sometimes during the main story you’ll need to buy items (such as books or school supplies) to advance, and Escape Bucks are the perfect system for that. This also ensures side quests become a more important part of the game, because we don’t care where the money comes from but we [i]can [/i]require that you engage with [i]some[/i] of the optional content, which gives the player a little more agency and further immersion at the Academy.[/p][p]                 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/d46648ba561aaca753899c163e32b07b378e3509.png"][/img][/p][p]Lastly, Escape Bucks can also be found in hidden nooks and crannies around the campus. So don’t be afraid to talk with every NPC and look underneath every stone, locker and toilet stall - just don’t go digging in other people’s pockets. That’s rude.[/p][p][/p][h1]What were some of the challenges with implementing quests?[/h1][p]It’s required a different look at the game design. Escape rooms want you to solve [i]everything[/i] very quickly, because it’s absolutely not fun to lose just because you went down a 10-minute rabbit hole exploring what would end up being a red herring.[/p][p]Quests, on the other hand, will allow a bit more freedom in the experience. This freedom can be a blessing and a curse - it’s definitely easier to design an escape room with some story inbetween, but quests require you to think out of the box in a way that might otherwise be limited with a linear room, and that’s just one of the many reasons we’re excited to continue fleshing out the quests system.[/p][p][/p][h1]What Do You Think?[/h1][p]We’re SUPER excited about this system because it fundamentally changes how you escape and lets the player deepen the bond they’ll feel with the Academy itself while playing.[/p][p] [/p][p]However, we want to hear your thoughts too! When it comes to quests, what are your expectations? Is there anything more you want to know? Drop your answers below, and don’t forget to…[/p][h1]     🔔[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2[/url]🔔[/h1][p] [/p][p]With love,[/p][p]Coin Crew Games 💛💜[/p]

notes.title: A (Sneak) Peek Behind The Curtain, and Some Transparency….
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Escapists!
[/h1][p]We know you’re just as excited as we are to get your hands on the next playtest build of [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Acadmey 2: Back 2 School[/url], so we’re bringing you an update with some of your most-asked questions, and a few peeks at what’s been going on at the Academy![/p][p] [/p][h1]I joined the Discord! When can I playtest?![/h1][p]We’re SO excited to start playtests (and on a personal note, [i]community manager to community[/i] - I am very excited to watch you all playtest the next build!) That’s why with much excitement, I’m here to tell you:[/p][p][/p][h1][i]Weekly Playtests are Kicking Off July 17th![/i][/h1][p] [/p][p]Keep your eyes peeled in our Discord, where you’ll be able to claim a spot for playtesting, and over there we’ll have more information on what you can expect out of the playtesting process.[/p][p] [/p][p]While you can’t playtest [i]right now[/i], there are a few other things you can do to satisfy your curiosity:[/p][olist][*][p]Check out our [url="https://tr.ee/T9jL-yt6JP"][b]socials![/b][/url] We’re constantly looking for new content to post, and with [b]playtests[/b] starting back up, you’ll be able to expect some sneak peeks, funny bugs, and more![/p][/*][*][p]Join the [b]Discord[/b]. There’s plenty of fun to be had, and you can say hi to your beloved [i]Coin Crew devs[/i] directly👋[/p][/*][*][p]Check out our other posts! We’re always looking for stuff to post, but if there’s something you’re wanting to see, it’s possible we’ve already posted it. [i]And if we haven’t…[/i].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Ask questions![/b] We’re just as excited to make this game as you are to play it, and hype keeps everyone motivated.[/p][/*][/olist][h1]Those Sneak Peeks We Were Promised!?[/h1][p]Our art team has been cooking up some really sick concepts for some other campuses at The Academy - after all, it’s more than just a school. It’s a thriving campus![/p][p] [/p][p]Here’s some work-in-progress concept art for the upcoming Science Campus you’ll be able to attend at Escape Academy. 📚What you see first are the grayboxed versions, followed by some paintover 🎨 sketches showing off how we plan to truly give these grayboxed environments life!😍[/p][p] [/p][p]We hope you enjoy this early look into the design process as much as we enjoy making it![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649515/020f43f26cc1425d05c97cb210ed7b4a1b5c9eef.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649515/185a355c658da77c4cf9c42dbb4960ba81a3515c.png"][/img][/p][p]                             ⚠️WIP! Expect this area to evolve and change in future iterations💛💜[/p][p][/p][h1]We want to know your questions![/h1][p]What do [i][b]YOU[/b][/i] want out of [i]Escape Academy 2[/i]? What are your wildest puzzle fantasies, or your weirdest escape-themed dreams? [i]Is having the ability to pick up the Purfessor a requirement for your enjoyment[/i]? Or maybe you REALLY want Gillian to be a bit more yappy?🤔[/p][p][/p][p]Whatever your asks are, we want our game to be a love letter to escape room games, fun puzzles, and purpose-built for our community to bash their heads into. Let us know what you’d like to see, and we’ll let you know what we think! The best way to reach us is always through [b]Discord[/b], but feel free to drop your thoughts anywhere you see us lurking around on the internet…⬇️[/p][p][/p][h1]🔔[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Wishlist Escape Academy 2![/url]🔔 [/h1][p][/p][p]With love,[/p][p][i]Coin Crew Games[/i] 💛💜[/p]

notes.title: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School Preview: An Entire World of Puzzles & Mystery
notes.content:
At Summer Game Fest 2025, we had a pile of “unannounced” appointments, which can be a gamble. Luckily, one of mine ended up being Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School, and the franchise has been a lot of fun so far, so I was excited to check out the latest version. I first played the original Escape Academy at Summer Game Fest 2022, so I felt good keeping the tradition alive.

I was originally paired with a stranger, which can make co-op puzzles a challenge, but they didn’t show up. So instead, I got to play a solid 30 minutes of Escape Academy 2 with none other than CGM’s own editor-in-chief, Brendan Frye. We sat down with an early section of the game, armed with a pen and paper, and proceeded to bicker publicly for the entire appointment—not much has changed.
